judge_assessment.explanation: The hard failure is factually wrong and it is the sole basis of the REJECT. It claims 'The Quick Answers bank prints 27 for item 10, which is Sam's planted wrong result; the requested correct value is 36 because 4/5 of 45 is 36.' Three independent artifacts refute it. (1) worksheet.tex line 102 reads 'Sam is asked for $\\frac{3}{5}$ of $45$ counters' — three fifths, not four fifths — and I rendered page 5 of worksheet.pdf at 130 dpi to confirm the typeset fraction is 3/5. The fraction 4/5 appears nowhere in the worksheet, the key, or the verification data, and 36 appears nowhere either. (2) 3/5 of 45 = 27, so 27 IS the requested correct value; answer_key.pdf's worked solution derives it as 45 ÷ 5 = 9 then 3 × 9 = 27 and boxes '27 counters', and verify.json id 10 is {type: eval, expr: 'a*n/b', at: {a: 3, b: 5, n: 45}, expected: 27}. (3) Sam's planted wrong result is 9, not 27: it is declared as a trap on the same entry — {desc: 'made the five equal groups but then took only one of them', expr: 'n/b', value: 9} — and the key prints it under 'Common wrong answers' as '10. If they got 9'. The worksheet text says so as well: 'points at one group, and says the answer is 9'. So the bank row '10. 27' is correct, agrees with the worked key, and agrees with the verifier. The judge's own critical observation ('the detailed item 10 solution correctly identifies 36') is likewise unsupported — the detailed solution identifies 27. mathematical_correctness 2 and answer_key_quality 2 rest on a misreading of one typeset fraction. Separately, item 10 does contain a real defect that the judge did not find: 'Write one sentence saying what he did right and what he forgot' is an open response, verify.json declares no manual entry anywhere in the file, and the gate summary reports all-green with no manual flag.

strengths_to_preserve: The two-move method (divide by the bottom to make the groups, multiply by the top to take some) is stated in the directions, modelled on every worked solution in the same order, and then deliberately broken by problem 10, where Sam performs move one correctly and stops. The key separates the halves explicitly: 'What he did right ... What he forgot ... His 9 is the answer to 1/5 of 45, not 3/5.'

The backwards items are built as a pair with different difficulty: problem 5 gives ONE part (1/5 is 8 grapes, so multiply by 5) and problem 9 gives THREE parts (3/8 is 96 people, so divide by 3 first, then multiply by 8), and problem 9's key names the trap that skipping that first step creates: 'dividing 96 by 8 to get 12. The 96 covers three parts, not one.'

Problem 8 attacks the read-the-question error rather than the arithmetic: 3/7 of 28 students ride the bus and the question asks how many do NOT, with the trap value 12 declared and the key adding a second route to the answer ('The students who do not ride are 4/7 of the class, and 4 × 4 = 16 as well').

Problem 7 keeps the same two moves when the set is a continuous quantity (1/8 of 2.4 litres = 0.3 L) and the trap 19.2 is refuted by a sense check a child can run: 'one glass cannot hold more than the whole jug'.

The drawn models are numerically faithful to the prose: I counted the TikZ loops in worksheet.tex and they give exactly 24 crayons (3×8), 21 stickers (3×7) and 45 counters (3×15), problem 5's bar has 4 dividers for 5 equal parts, and problem 9's bar is shaded 0 to 3.375 of 9, i.e. exactly three eighths.

root_causes.description: The REJECT was produced by a judging error, not by an artifact defect. The judge read problem 10's typeset \\frac{3}{5} as a different fraction, computed 4/5 of 45 = 36, and then declared the correct answer 27 to be 'Sam's planted wrong result' — which the same problem's own trap declaration contradicts. Nothing in the judging protocol requires a hard failure that asserts a corrected value to be cross-checked against the artifacts, so an asserted 'correct value' that appears in no file (36) and a misattributed 'planted wrong result' both passed into the official score, costing four rubric points across two dimensions.
evidence: worksheet.tex line 102: 'Sam is asked for $\\frac{3}{5}$ of $45$ counters.' Rendered page 5 of worksheet.pdf confirms 3/5.
verify.json id 10: expected 27, with a declared trap {expr: 'n/b', value: 9, desc: 'made the five equal groups but then took only one of them'}.
answer_key.pdf item 10 boxes '27 counters' and lists under Common wrong answers: '10. If they got 9: made the five equal groups but then took only one of them'.
The strings '36' and '4/5' occur nowhere in worksheet.tex, answer_key.tex, verify.json or verify_study_guide.json for this task.

root_causes.description: The sheet declares no manual items while printing one written explanation and six drawn or labelled responses. Problem 10's 'write one sentence saying what he did right and what he forgot' is the clearest, and the answer key even supplies grading guidance for it ('Full credit on the sentence: it has to name both halves') without any corresponding manual entry, so the machine record says the sheet is fully auto-gradable when the key itself knows it is not.
evidence: worksheet.pdf problem 10 asks for one sentence before the correct answer; verify.json contains no entry with "type": "manual".
answer_key.pdf item 10: 'Full credit on the sentence: it has to name both halves ... “He got it wrong” does not show that the student can see where the method broke.'

worksheet.pdf problems 1, 2 ('Circle'/'Ring the equal groups'), 3, 4 ('split ... write how many marbles are in one part ... then shade'), 5 ('Write 8 in each part') and 9 all require drawn or written-on work that nothing records.
gate_log.txt: 'verify-ws PASS ... ✅ BUILD PASSED — all gates green'; the machine observation records gate_chain_manual_flags false.

root_causes.description: Several problems print an intermediate value as its own response slot and only the final value is verified. Problem 9 asks for the size of one eighth AND the total, and only 256 is checked; problem 3 asks the student to write how many marbles are in one part before shading; problem 4 asks them to label one part. The one-part values (32, 6, 8) are exactly the quantities that separate a child who understands the model from one who guessed the total.
evidence: worksheet.pdf problem 9: 'Work out how many seats one eighth holds, then find how many seats the theatre has altogether.' verify.json id 9: solve('3*n/8 - 96') = [256] only; the key derives 96 ÷ 3 = 32 as a separate boxed step.
worksheet.pdf problem 3: '... write how many marbles are in one part, then shade the parts the top number asks for.' verify.json id 3 verifies only 12.

worksheet.pdf problem 4: 'Split the bar into equal parts, label one part, and shade what Dev has read.' verify.json id 4 verifies only 24 — and the label value 8 is declared as a TRAP for the final answer, so the same number is a required intermediate response and a flagged wrong answer.

improvements.title: A judge's hard failure that asserts a corrected value must cite text present in the artifacts, and the harness should flag one that does not
improvements.proposed_change: Amend evals/curriculum-judge-rubric.md so that any hard failure of the form 'the key prints X where the correct answer is Y' must quote the problem stem verbatim from the rendered PDF and name the verify.json entry it contradicts, and must state the arithmetic that produces Y from the quoted givens. Add a mechanical guard at aggregate time in evals/score_eval.py: extract numeric literals and fractions from each hard_failure string and warn when a literal asserted as the correct value occurs in none of worksheet.tex, answer_key.tex, verify.json or verify_study_guide.json for that task. A warning does not overturn a verdict — it routes the verdict to a second look before it enters the run report, which is all that was needed here.
improvements.regression_test: Feed the aggregate guard curr-131's task directory together with its hard_failure string 'the requested correct value is 36 because 4/5 of 45 is 36'. The guard must flag the verdict, because neither '36' nor '4/5' occurs in any artifact for curr-131. Feed it curr-103's hard failure ('prints 4600, 4600, — rather than ... 4550 and 4649') and it must NOT flag, because 4550, 4649 and 4600 all occur in curr-103's artifacts. Both assertions fail today, since no such guard exists.
improvements.expected_impact: Catches the exact failure that cost this task four rubric points and a REJECT, and generalises to any judging error that invents a value. It is cheap: a string scan over files the harness already reads.
improvements.risk: Numeric extraction will produce false positives for values that are legitimately derived rather than printed (an intermediate a judge computed correctly), so the guard must warn and route for review, never auto-overturn. It also must not be readable as pressure on the judge to defer to the artifacts — the point is to make a disagreement explicit and checked, not to suppress it.

improvements.title: Problem 10's written sentence, and the drawn work in problems 1-5 and 9, are recorded as fully machine-verified
improvements.proposed_change: Require a manual entry whenever a problem body contains an explanation imperative ('write one sentence saying ...', 'explain', 'why') or a drawing imperative ('circle', 'ring', 'shade', 'split the bar', 'label', 'write 8 in each part'), enforced as a gate lint over the worksheet source. Where the answer key already contains grading guidance — as item 10's 'Full credit on the sentence' does — the absence of a matching manual entry should be a hard error, since the document is contradicting its own machine record.
improvements.regression_test: Fixture with curr-131's problem 10 text plus the key's 'Full credit on the sentence' paragraph and a verify.json holding only the eval 3×45/5 = 27. The lint must exit non-zero on the missing manual entry; adding {id: 10, type: 'manual', desc: 'Explain what Sam did right and what he forgot'} must make it pass and must flip the gate summary from all-green to verify-ws MANUAL.
improvements.expected_impact: Makes this concept-models sheet report its real review burden — one written sentence and six drawn responses — instead of claiming full automatic coverage, and satisfies the prompt's labelling clause.
improvements.risk: Restrict scanning to problem bodies; the directions block here says 'Draw or circle the groups before you write any numbers' and would otherwise trigger on every problem.

improvements.title: Problem 9 prints two requested numbers and verifies one; problems 3 and 4 print an intermediate the student must write and verify only the total
improvements.proposed_change: Count each conjoined request inside a problem as its own slot and require an entry for each. For problem 9 that means adding {type: 'eval', expr: 'p/k', at: {p: 96, k: 3}, expected: 32} beside the solve for 256, so the bank row reads '32, 256'; for problems 3 and 4, add the one-part values 6 and 8 as their own entries. Where a one-part value is also declared as a trap for the FINAL answer (problem 4's 8), the schema should require the trap and the intermediate to be distinguished so the key does not list a required intermediate response as a wrong answer without qualification.
improvements.regression_test: Fixture with curr-131's problem 9 (two slots) and a verify.json holding only solve('3*n/8 - 96') = [256]. tests/check_answer_key.py must report the uncovered one-eighth slot; adding the eval for 32 must pass and must render the bank row as '9.~32, 256'.
improvements.expected_impact: The one-part value is the quantity that distinguishes understanding the model from guessing the total, and on a guided concept sheet it is the number a parent most needs beside the answer. Fixes three rows here and the same pattern across the visual-model band.
improvements.risk: More entries per problem lengthen the bank rows and can push render_quick_answers' adaptive column count down to two, so the layout guard should be re-checked on the longest sheets.

case_summary: The REJECT should not stand and I disagree with the judge on the record. The hard failure says the bank prints Sam's planted wrong result 27 where the correct value is 36 'because 4/5 of 45 is 36'; the worksheet asks for 3/5 of 45 (worksheet.tex line 102, confirmed by rendering page 5), 3/5 of 45 is 27, the key derives and boxes 27, verify.json expects 27, and Sam's planted wrong result is 9 — declared as a trap and printed in the key as 'If they got 9'. Neither 36 nor 4/5 occurs anywhere in this task's artifacts. Four rubric points across mathematical_correctness and answer_key_quality rest on a misread fraction. The sheet itself is strong: the divide-then-multiply method is stated, modelled and then deliberately broken in problem 10; the backwards items 5 and 9 are graded one-part versus three-part; the read-the-question trap in problem 8 is declared; and every hand-drawn model's count matches its prose. Its real defects, which the judge did not find, are coverage ones: no manual entry for problem 10's written sentence (despite the key printing grading guidance for it) or for the six drawn responses, and problem 9's one-eighth value, problem 3's one-part value and problem 4's labelled part are printed slots that nothing verifies.
